# Developer Training And Support

## API Reference - REST

Avetta provides access to select business objects through a set of RESTful APIs. In this portal you will find a list of the available endpoints with the latest information. For more information about a particular endpoint, click on it in the left pane to view a description of the endpoint and any query parameters. The mock testing feature will show a sample response payload.

## Help Centre

To search the Help Centre for guides related to API usage, navigate to the relevant section depending on your product:  

[Connect](https://help.avetta.com/s/topic/0TO4u000000w8heGAA/connect-platform-application-program-interface-apis?tabset-b9e8a=2) 

[Worker Management]( https://help.avetta.com/s/topic/0TO4u000000w8hhGAA/worker-management-platform-application-program-interface-apis?language=en_US&tabset-b9e8a=2) 

[Pegasus Work Force Management]( https://help.avetta.com/s/topic/0TO4u000000w8iMGAQ/workforce-management-platform-application-program-interface-apis?language=en_US&tabset-b9e8a=2) 

## Support 

For additional support contact apisupport@avetta.com and/or your Account Manager.

# Getting Started

## Scopes
Many Onsite API paths require parameters named scopeId or siteId to identify the target within Onsite. The values relevant to you will be supplied by your Project Manager or can be found using the API below. Your setup may have other locations and sub-location that will have their own scopeId’s that can be found using the above siteId and an existing endpoint in the Site Location Controller if required.

To use the APIs, you will need a scope ID to return the data associated with the scope you are interrogating.

Get Current User Top Level Scopes

This endpoint will return the scope ID’s that your user account has access to.

Workforce Management Environments
The base URL will depend on which API you are requesting, as well as which instance your Avetta application has been created with.

### Test
The test environment is called the Emulated Production Environment (EPE) Access to EPE is for testing purposes only, and data is reset on a regular basis. The base URL for requests to this environment looks like this:

https://epe.onsitetrackeasy.com.au/onsite-rest.

### Production
The live environment is called the Production Environment (API). Access to Production is subject to an API agreement and payment terms. The base URL for requests to this environment looks like this:

https://epe.onsitetrackeasy.com.au/onsite-rest.

## Authentication
Workforce Management API uses two alternative authentication schemes to authenticate all requests and post via the API framework. An integration user account must be created by the Workforce management Account Manager prior to any testing or implementation. This integration user account relates specifically to the external system keys and it’s ability to modify employee data in Workforce Management relating to that external system. A username and password will be created and supplied to all API clients based on their system requirements and licensing arrangements.

### Methodologies
Using the “login-controller” end point, clients submit their username and password in order to retrieve an Oauth 2.0 Bearer token, supplied in the header
A long lived API-Key is provided by the Account Manager and then used in all HTTP requests in the header to authenticate each request.

# Common Use Cases

## Access Control Integration
The Onsite Workforce Management APIs provide solutions for company pre-qualification and management of workers’ competencies to ensure that they compliant and prepared to safely work on site. Additionally, Avetta supplies access control solutions including kiosks, tablets, turnstiles, boom gates and secure doors which leverage this data to ensure only authorised workers can access site.

Some clients have already invested significantly in 3rd party access control solutions and would like to be able to integrate the data from the Onsite Verification Engine into their own systems. This can be achieved by integrating with the Onsite Rest Endpoints.  

The aim of this case study is to provide a high-level overview of how the Onsite APIs can used to identify workers that are authorised to access client sites.  This information can then be replicated to the third-party access control system to ensure only authorised people can access site.  

### WORKFLOW – ACCESS CONTROL
The workflow is as follows:

* Companies and Workers become compliant for work at 1 or more sites in the onsite system.
* The client middleware server authenticates and then can call the Pegasus Rest endpoints allowing the client middleware server to retrieve the compliant workers for that client site or project.
* The client access control server then propagates this data out to the individual client sites.
* The client middleware server calls the Pegasus endpoints and retrieves ongoing changes every 1 hour. Typically, the changes would be if a new person has become compliant for a site, if a person has had their access revoked or if a person has become non-compliant.

The useful endpoints are as follows:

* [Get competencies by personId](#tag/scope-person-competency-controller/operation/getPersonCompetencies)
* [Get comptencies by id with External ID](#tag/scope-person-competency-client-controller/operation/getPersonCompetencies_1)
* Alternatively [Get person competency for competencyId](#tag/scope-person-competency-controller/operation/getPersonCompetency) when you have a known competencyId within the gate system to check.
* [Get person competency currency](#tag/scope-person-competency-controller/operation/getPersonCompetencyCurrency) to return a simple true|false to establish whether competency has expired.
* [Get competency assignment changes](#tag/scope-competency-assignment-controller/operation/getChanges) to show when employees have been assignment to a competency (but not necessarily completed it).

## Competency Integration
The Onsite Workforce Management APIs provide solutions for company pre-qualification and management of workers’ competencies to ensure that they compliant and prepared to safely work on site.

Some clients have already invested significantly in 3rd party access Learning Management System solutions and would like to be able to integrate the data from the Onsite Training Engine into their own systems (and vice versa. This can be achieved by integrating with the Onsite Rest Endpoints.  

The aim of this case study is to provide a high-level overview of how the Onsite APIs can used to push data about completed training to the onsite portal, to ensure correct access to site and workforce management.   

Assign Competency To Worker
Update Comptency Assignment

## Workforce Management Data with HR Systems
Systems external to the Pegasus Onsite Workforce Management can be synced with the available employee data. This typically aligns to most common implementation of Employee and HR management systems for onboarding, updating, and terminating employees in Avetta Workforce Management.

Commonly the HR system is the master system for employee data and allows clients to update employee data and for this information to be replicated in Pegasus however not used exclusively for this purpose.

### Prerequisite - External System Key Setup
It is common that external HR and Employee management systems have an existing employee Identifier. This in most cases is linked to payroll or other internal systems. As a result, this existing employee identifier can be used as a reference lookup in Pegasus to maintain employee contacts. These employee identifiers are created as external identifiers in the Pegasus system. An external identifier must be setup by Pegasus Development Team prior to any integration system. External Identifiers comprise of the following components:

| ELEMENT |	DESCRIPTION |
| ------------- |-------------|
| extSysKey	| Refers to the “External System Key”. This typically identifies the system in which the employee master data resides (EG SAP, WORKDAY, Success Factors). This is a UUID that is given to the client by Pegasus and assigned to all employee records. |
| idKey |This is the unique identifier of the employee in the master system. |
| Name | Name of the external system id field (EG “Payroll ID”, “SAP Number”) |

*Identifiers and Data Seeding*
Once the external system ID has been created. This will appear in onsite track easy under the employee profile as a new field to be populated. This can be manually entered into the system by :

* Login to onsite track easy (https://secure.onsitetrackeasy.com.au )
* Go to employee menu
* Search an employee
* Click their name to view profile
* Click edit to edit their values
* Enter the external ID into the new field created and press save.
* All existing employees must have their external ID fields populated prior to any integration as to avoid and duplicate profiles. Once these ID’s are created Pegasus Dev must run a bulk update script on existing employees to populate the “extSysKey” relating to those employee ID values. Once this is done then updates may occur using the external system ID value via the following employee API endpoints.

### Interacting With Employee/Contractor Data
Data can be synchronised both ways with the Pegasus/Onsite APIs. An example use case might involve the following data flows:

To provision efficient client facing API for the delivery of data between Pegasus and and external system for:

#### INBOUND (External to Pegasus)
* Onboarding - Employee
* Offboarding Employee
* Cross boarding Employee
* Updated Employee details
* Updated Next of Kin (Employee)
* Offboarding Managed Contractor
### OUTBOUND (Pegasus to External)
* Onboarding Managed Contractor - poll for new contractor records
* Cross boarding Managed Contractor
* Updated Managed Contractor
* Updated Next of Kin (Managed contractor)
* The capability to be able to GET all user (worker) records from Onsite in a single API call (with pagination if required) – Less frequent – frequency to be determined.
* Integrating Managed Contractors
* A worker may be an employee, and therefore associated with a single main company code (belonging to the integrating company), or they may be a "managed contractor". A worker must be associated with a company, and the company must be associated to the realm the API integration is working with. The workflow for integrating "managed contractors" is therefore as follows:

The useful endpoints for this workflow are as follows:

* Find Company
* Register Company
* Integrate Worker
* Add Employee (Add Company to Worker)
* Find Updated Contractors
* Find Workers
* Add Site Association to Worker
* Remove Site Association from Worker
